selected_evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
selected_evidence.summary: Created and validated /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-commands-log with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log; log file shows timestamped entries with user and command for each sudo invocation

selected_evidence.requirement: entries kept out of the general system log (auth.log/syslog)
selected_evidence.summary: Test user sudologtest ran a sudo command; entry appeared in sudo-commands.log with user=sudologtest, and grep for that user/command in auth.log returned 0 matches, confirming syslog suppression via Defaults !syslog
Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, uptime, sudoers config content, and 49-line log file count before reboot
Issued sudo shutdown -r now via backgrounded nohup; command returned exit 0 before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: changed boot identity proves actual restart
selected_evidence.summary: Node briefly unreachable (connection timed out) then returned with boot_id 3e90fb02-9cc0-4fef-a228-13a3153406aa (different from baseline) and uptime 4.02s

selected_evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and correct log routing
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers snippet intact, sudo-commands.log continued growing with new timestamped entries, and grep of auth.log COMMAND= lines showed only pre-fix entries (hostname still 'ubuntu24', all timestamps <=11:17:18) with zero new command entries post-reboot
